ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and continuously thereafter, screen all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, customers, suppliers, logistics counterparties, banks, customs agents, and identified beneficial owners against United Nations sanctions, applicable European Union restrictive measures, Spanish domestic sanctions and law-enforcement information, OFAC lists where relevant to the transaction or payment chain, and reputable PEP and adverse-media databases. Obtain source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence for higher-risk parties, assess ownership and control of sanctioned entities, document false-positive resolution, apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs and close associates, prohibit transactions involving sanctioned parties, and retain AML records for the statutory period under Law 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central, official name-clearance service available through https://www.rmc.es and the Registradores de España electronic platform at https://sede.registradores.org
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in the Latin alphabet and contain the legal-form designation or accepted abbreviation, including Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, S.L., or equivalent permitted form. The name must be sufficiently distinct from existing registered names, must not be misleading, and may not improperly use protected public, governmental, geographic, regulated-sector, or trademark designations. Spanish is accepted; names in other languages or scripts may require explanatory translation, transliteration, or registry acceptance. A separate trademark clearance is required because company-name registration does not create trademark rights.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Aduana or Customs terms suggesting official status
Europeo or European terms implying official governmental status
Official emblems, royal references, and names of public authorities
Any protected trademark, regulated professional designation, or term requiring sectoral authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File the name-clearance application with the Registro Mercantil Central using several alternative names and the exact intended legal-form designation. After issuance, the negative name certificate is generally usable for incorporation for three months, while the name is reserved for six months. If rejected, obtain the written grounds, compare the proposed name against the registry's similarity and protected-term criteria, submit a replacement application or request rectification through the Registro Mercantil Central's available administrative channel, and preserve the electronic filing receipt. A legally defective or improperly reasoned registry decision may be challenged through the applicable administrative and contentious-administrative remedies; professional review is required because the appropriate remedy and deadline depend on the decision served.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office must correspond to the company's real administrative and management address and remain available for official notices. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable for a holding or administrative company only if it provides genuine mail handling, document access, and compliance support. It cannot replace the physical premises required for bonded warehousing, customs control, inventory custody, security, access control, records, and inspection. The company must separately secure an approved customs facility or authorization under the Union Customs Code and Spanish customs procedures. For this business, a virtual office alone is not commercially or regulatory sufficient.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official statistical probability is published. Qualitative risk is high for the operational warehouse and medium for the registered office because bonded or customs-controlled facilities are subject to customs supervision, authorization checks, record reviews, inventory verification, and possible announced or unannounced inspections. The business plan should assume inspection at any time permitted by customs legislation and should maintain physical premises, access logs, stock records, security controls, and responsible personnel.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada), Articles 19-22 (share capital), 22-31 (incorporation deed and registration), 62 (administrators), and 209 (registered office).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is established, under the coordination of the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) executed before a notary and filed electronically with the Mercantile Registry via the Colegio de Registradores de la Propiedad, Bienes Muebles y Mercantiles de España.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada requires a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid up at formation. Payment must be evidenced by a bank certificate or notarial statement of deposit; no escrow account is required for cash contributions, but non-cash contributions require independent expert valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a duly convened meeting of the founding members of Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada ES_SL, it was resolved: (1) the share capital of EUR 3,000 is hereby subscribed and fully paid by the founding partners, and the attached bank certificate of deposit is approved; (2) the registered office is fixed at the address stated in the articles, within the jurisdiction of the relevant Mercantile Registry; (3) the administration is entrusted to a sole administrator, appointed with a five-year term; (4) the administrator is authorised to execute the public deed, apply for the tax identification number, and initiate all operating licences; (5) all prior resolutions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the pre-emptive certificate of name registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Mercantile Registry), Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit digital application through the Registro Mercantil Central online portal requesting certification that the proposed company name (denominación social) is not identical to any existing name. Provide three alternative names in order of preference. Pay prescribed fee via electronic transfer or card. The positive certification is valid for 3 months and must be annexed to the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Passport or NIE copies of all founding members
Proof of payment of the certification fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried because of similitude, file a fresh request with amended name alternatives within the validity period; or file an administrative appeal before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública if the refusal is considered incorrect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a provisional bank account and deposit share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution selected by the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the deed of incorporation in escrow? No. Actually: open a temporary account in the name of the company in formation (sociedad en formación), deposit the minimum EUR 3,000, and obtain a bank certificate (certificado de depósito) stating the deposit, account number, and holder. The certificate must be dated within two months prior to the deed date.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening due to enhanced due diligence, request a written refusal and submit to another bank; or the partners may pay up capital via notarial deposit with the Notary's cooperative account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the statutory incorporation deed before a notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (Notario) in the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with the name certificate, bank deposit certificate, draft articles (estatutos), NIE/passport of all founders, and tax identification numbers. The notary will read the deed, verify identities, receive consent, and issue the authorized first copy (copia autorizada) plus protocol number. The deed must state the partners, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, and administration structure.
required_dossiers: Positive name certificate from Registro Mercantil Central
Bank certificate of share capital deposit
Original passports/NIE cards of all founding members
Spanish tax identification numbers (NIF) of foreign founders, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires additional clauses or identifies omissions, amend the draft articles and re-execute the deed as a public deed of rectification or execute a private supplementary document before the same notary before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for the provisional NIF and pay the transfer and stamp tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Local Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 business days after deed execution, file Form 036 to request the provisional Tax Identification Number (código de identificación fiscal, NIF provisional) and simultaneously declare the incorporation for Capital Transfer and Stamp Duty (ITPAJD) under Article 31 of the consolidated ITP Law at the box/office that has territorial jurisdiction. Pay the respective tax on the formation transaction (exempt for SL in many regions? Actually 1% on capital for SL subject to OJ? Wait, capital operations tax: 1% on paid-up capital for limited liability companies if in Spain; many autonomias have bonuses). Use official receipt.
required_dossiers: Notarial first copy or simple copy of the deed
NIE/passports of the administrators and partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the provisional NIF is queried because of errors in the deed or the ITPAJD payment cannot be matched, correct the administrative error, resubmit the form, and present the treasury receipt to the local AEAT office for manual validation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company with the Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial corresponding to the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first copy of the notarial deed together with the provisional NIF certificate and payment evidence of ITPAJD at the Mercantile Registry. The registry verifies the legality of the deed and enters the company in the Commercial Register. After registration, the company acquires legal personality.
required_dossiers: First authorized copy of the incorporation deed
Copy or original of the provisional NIF certificate
ITPAJD proof of payment (Form 600 with receipt)
Name certificate used in the deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a nota de calificación suspending registration, the notary or interested parties must comply with the defects noted (e.g., amend articles, supply missing documentation) and request re-presentation within the legal term or file a recourse before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the incorporation in the Official Gazette and obtain the definitive NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME) and Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Mercantile Registry transmits the company's registered particulars to BORME for publication. Concurrently, file Form 036 with AEAT to convert the provisional NIF to the definitive NIF and obtain the company's definitive tax identification number. After this step, company may open final bank accounts and invoice.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If BORME publication is delayed or contains errors, request rectification from the register or the BORME administration; if AEAT queries the definitive NIF, present the registration certificate and pay any outstanding ITPAJD before requesting re-issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File for the electronic signature certificate and company activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Fábrica Nacional de Moneda y Timbre (FNMT-RCM) / AEAT electronic registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After definitive NIF, obtain a company digital certificate (certificado electrónico) or use chip pin by the legal representative. Register the company in the AEAT Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores, and set up the electronic address (Dirección Electrónica Habilitada) for official notifications.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate application is rejected, correct the data, obtain a new single-use code at the provincial revenue office, and reapply; for the administrative census, file written request and wait for assignment of activation status.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales of AEAT jointly with the relevant Free Trade Zone Consortium (Consorcio de la Zona Franca) under the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización de Deposito Aduanero o de Depósito Distinto del aduanero en Zona Franca (Customs Bonded Warehouse Authorisation for Free Trade Zone Operators), including compliance with the Ley de Zonas Francas (Law 18/2014) and the Customs Regulation UCC/2013/952

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Consejería de Medio Ambiente of the Autonomous Community where the warehouse is located; for cross-community projects the Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Simplified Environmental Impact Assessment (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental simplificado) if the warehouse occupies > 10,000 m² or stores hazardous goods; otherwise Category C – Environmental Licence (Licencia ambiental) registration or environmental communication. Bonded storage of general goods is usually exempt from full EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with urban wastewater discharge limits (RD 509/1996, annexes), wastewater discharge permit thresholds for BOD5 < 300 mg/l, COD < 500 mg/l, total suspended solids < 300 mg/l, pH 6-9; fugitive VOC emissions below 10 mg/Nm³ as per Directive 2010/75/EU on Industrial Emissions; waste handling in compliance with Ley 7/2022 on waste and circular economy, maintaining hazardous waste manifests and disposal permits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate granted by the local municipal technical service or the Fire Services of the Autonomous Community after inspection (basic fire protection measures per CTE DB SI), structural load compliance certificate for the warehouse issued by a competent technician, and occupational safety clearance under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales, including initial risk assessment, fire drill plan, emergency evacuation plan, and evidence of an occupational health service

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); central electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es). Customs, excise and free-zone/bonded warehouse control are administered by the AEAT Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales. Spain is a unitary tax jurisdiction with no sub-central VAT or corporate income tax authorities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An SL must obtain a Spanish tax ID (NIF, in CIF format for legal entities) before formal incorporation: the notary requests a provisional NIF certificate from AEAT; after the deed of incorporation is filed in the Registro Mercantil, the definitive NIF is issued through Form 036/037 using electronic certification. Foreign non-resident shareholders, directors and fiscal representatives must be reported via the same forms. For bonded depot / free-zone operations the SL additionally requires: (i) an EORI number in the format ES + NIF for all customs transactions; (ii) a customs authorization for a free-zone or customs warehouse (Depósito Aduanero) under the Union Customs Code, including an approved storage system and a customs guarantee bond; and (iii) an AEAT electronic certificate (FNMT or qualified provider) for all e-filing, SII transmission and customs EDI/DUA clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SL is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Spanish Corporate Income Tax, Ley 27/2014) at the general rate of 25% (15% for newly created SLs with positive result in the first two tax periods, subject to turnover and activity conditions). Profits are taxed at entity level; shareholders are not treated as transparent. VAT treatment for free-zone and bonded warehouse activities is governed by the territorial and suspension rules of Ley 37/1992 (IVA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a check-the-box or US-style entity classification election. Pass-through treatment is available only for statutorily transparent vehicles such as UTEs (Unión Temporal de Empresas), AIEs (Agrupaciones de Interés Económico) and European EEIGs; an SL cannot elect to be treated as transparent for tax. Relevant elective or special regimes for this profile include: (i) reduced 15% corporate income tax rate for newly incorporated SLs meeting legal thresholds; (ii) optional application of the customs suspensive regime for free zones and bonded warehouses (this is a customs authorization, not an income tax election); (iii) VAT group election for closely linked entities where applicable; (iv) corporate income tax group consolidation election (art. 61 LIS) for groups with at least 70% direct or indirect holding; and (v) statutory hybrid mismatch rules transposing ATAD (Law 11/2021) which disallow elective outcomes that exploit double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA) — Spanish Value Added Tax, governed by Ley 37/1992 del IVA and RD 1624/1992, harmonised with the EU VAT Directive.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None — registration is mandatory from the first taxable economic activity in Spain, regardless of turnover; any SL or non-resident operator making taxable supplies in Spanish territory must register via Form 036/037 (with prior EORI for customs activities). The simplified VAT regime for small retailers is capped by an annual volume of operations below EUR 250,000 but is not available to free-zone operators, storage providers or customs warehouse operators.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic fiscal reporting and clearance: (i) SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) requires taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, and VAT groups, to transmit invoice records in XML/API format to AEAT within 4 calendar days of issue (8 days for invoices received via counterparty records); (ii) the Verifactu framework requires billing software to guarantee authenticity and integrity; (iii) Spain has no mechanical digital stamping model for VAT, the fiscal anchor being SII and Verifactu; (iv) Ley 18/2022 ('Crea y Crece') will make B2B electronic invoicing (Facturae / UBL 2.1 format) mandatory on a phased schedule once the implementing regulation enters into force; and (v) all free-zone and bonded-depot customs operations require electronic clearance through AEAT customs EDI/XML systems, with the DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) filed digitally for each import, suspension entry and export movement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated IVA applies to exports of goods to non-EU destinations under art. 21 Ley 37/1992, provided: (i) the goods physically leave EU customs territory within 3 months of the supply; (ii) the supplier retains the status of exporter in the electronic DUA; and (iii) documentary proof of dispatch and destination is maintained. Goods placed in a free zone or bonded depot are outside the scope of Spanish IVA while under the suspensive customs regime (art. 23 Ley IVA); IVA becomes zero-rated at the moment of final export, and the right to deduct input VAT is preserved when the export conditions are substantiated. Services directly connected with the export (loading, handling, storage in the bonded facility, customs clearance and transport) are also zero-rated under art. 21.7 when performed for the non-resident owner of the goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA) electronically accepted by AEAT, evidencing the free-zone/bonded-depot exit and the export destination outside the EU
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (with CMR for road exports) proving physical dispatch and arrival in the non-EU destination customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate — bank or payment-provider documentation proving receipt of the export proceeds and compliance with the FX repatriation obligation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT cross-matches SII invoice records, customs DUA data and bank FX receipts to detect abusive zero-rating. Unsubstantiated export claims trigger: (i) reassessment of undeclared IVA with late-payment interest (interés de demora) and enforcement surcharges (recargo de apremio: 5% ordinary, 10%-20% protested); (ii) penalties under art. 194 LGT for obtaining undue refunds or tax benefits: 50% for serious infringements, 100% for very serious infringements involving false or falsified invoices, and 150% where fraudulent concealment means are used; (iii) loss of input VAT deduction and retrospective clawback within the 4-year statutory assessment window (period is suspended while tax-crime investigations are pending); and (iv) criminal liability under art. 305/305 bis Código Penal for tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000, with imprisonment of 1 to 6 years and fines of up to six times the defrauded amount, plus customs penalty proceedings for false declarations and possible joint liability of directors and legal representatives.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) is Spain's central bank and participates in the Eurosystem. The European Central Bank sets euro-area monetary policy. The Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT), including its customs authorities, administers customs, tax, and applicable foreign-trade formalities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies the EU framework for free movement of capital and payments. The euro is fully convertible, and there is generally no exchange-control approval or mandatory conversion for ordinary current-account or capital-account payments. Cross-border dividends, interest, service fees, loan repayments, and capital transactions are not subject to a general Spanish profit-repatriation quota, but remain subject to corporate-law procedures, tax withholding and treaty rules, transfer-pricing requirements where relevant, sanctions, AML controls, and bank documentation. Payments involving non-EU jurisdictions may require additional sanctions, tax, statistical, or bank review. Cash and bearer negotiable instruments crossing EU external borders are subject to applicable EU and Spanish declaration requirements. Spanish residents and payment-service providers may have Banco de España statistical reporting obligations for external transactions; the responsible reporting party and thresholds should be confirmed against current Banco de España rules and the transaction channel.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory deadline requiring export proceeds to be repatriated and no mandatory surrender or conversion ratio. Export receipts may generally be retained in foreign-currency accounts, subject to the company's accounting, tax, AML, sanctions, and any applicable statistical reporting obligations. Retain sales contracts, invoices, transport and customs records, proof of export or customs status, and bank remittance evidence. Exporters should separately assess VAT zero-rating or exemption substantiation and any customs, excise, or bonded-warehouse conditions; customs procedures do not create a general FX surrender obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for routine SEPA and supported international payments, subject to the provider's country, currency, sector, and customer acceptance policies. An EU-licensed electronic money institution or payment institution may provide regulated payment services under its authorization and applicable passporting rules, but an EMI account is not automatically a bank deposit, does not necessarily provide deposit-guarantee protection, and may not support capital formation, customs guarantees, trade finance, cash handling, or bonded-warehouse operational needs. An offshore provider without the required EU/Spanish authorization or lawful passporting cannot be assumed to provide regulated services in Spain. Maintain a Spanish bank relationship for tax, customs, payroll, guarantees, and resilient treasury operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that every director appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be available at the institution's discretion using accepted electronic identification and qualified electronic signatures. Banks may require an in-person meeting, original or legalized documents, Spanish tax identification numbers, or additional verification, particularly for non-resident directors, complex ownership, high-risk jurisdictions, or cash-intensive logistics. Confirm requirements with the selected bank before incorporation or funding; a notarial power of attorney may be accepted only if the bank approves its form and authentication.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership, nominee arrangements, trusts, or inability to identify natural-person beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current ownership chart to natural persons; shareholder register and corporate registry extracts; constitutional documents; beneficial-owner declarations and applicable Spanish beneficial-ownership filings; identity and address evidence; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; explanations and supporting records for any trust, nominee, or intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or directors, high-risk-country connections, sanctions exposure, or politically exposed persons
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified identity and address records; tax-residence details; full ownership and control chart; sanctions and PEP screening information; source-of-wealth evidence; transaction rationale; counterparty and country risk assessment; applicable licenses or legal opinions; enhanced due-diligence responses requested by the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or unexplained initial capital contribution, third-party funding, shareholder loans, or transfers inconsistent with the business plan
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan documents; board and shareholder resolutions; originating account statements; proof of beneficial ownership of source accounts; audited or tax records evidencing accumulated funds; funding-flow diagram; payment purpose and accounting treatment; bank transfer confirmations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Customs-free-zone, bonded-depot, or warehouse activity with unclear authorization, goods origin, counterparties, or payment flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AEAT customs authorization and relevant customs procedure approvals; warehouse or free-zone operator agreements; premises and insurance evidence; customs guarantee details; inventory-control and audit procedures; sample customer and supplier contracts; invoices, transport documents, customs declarations, goods-origin records, sanctions screening controls, and a documented flow of goods and funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive operations, unusual payment layering, third-party collections, rapid pass-through transfers, or mismatch between declared turnover and account activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Expected-volume and transaction-profile schedule; customer and supplier due-diligence files; invoice-to-payment reconciliations; warehouse receipts and inventory records; cash-handling policy; payment authorization matrix; bank-account ownership evidence; explanation and documentary trail for intercompany and third-party payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing Spanish corporate, tax, or signing-authority documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed of incorporation and amendments; current Mercantile Registry certificate or extract; Spanish tax identification number (NIF); bylaws; appointment and powers of directors and authorized signatories; board resolutions; beneficial-owner information; registered office evidence; and certified translations, apostilles, or legalization where required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through an account held in the investor's or documented funding entity's name to the SL's Spanish bank account, with the transfer reference matching the subscription, capital increase, or shareholder-loan documentation. Obtain corporate approvals and execute the required notarial and Mercantile Registry formalities for capital transactions. Provide the bank with the investor identity and ownership chain, source-of-funds evidence, subscription or loan agreement, resolutions, and intended accounting treatment. Use the correct bank payment-purpose information and any applicable Banco de España statistical reporting classification; there is no universal Spanish FX purpose-code regime for ordinary transfers. Do not characterize debt as equity or use unrelated third-party accounts. For customs guarantees or operational liquidity, arrange a separate facility and confirm acceptable collateral and beneficiary requirements with AEAT and the bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the scheme limits and availability; use SWIFT customer credit transfers, commonly documented through MT103-format information or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. Provide accurate beneficiary, bank, invoice, contract, shipment, customs, and payment-purpose details, and retain remittance and reconciliation records. For supplier settlements requiring documentary protection, arrange a documentary commercial letter of credit, documentary collection, or bank guarantee subject to the agreed rules and bank credit approval. Match payment terms to Incoterms, title and risk transfer, customs status, VAT treatment, and warehouse records. Screen counterparties, beneficial owners, vessels, goods, and jurisdictions for sanctions and export-control restrictions before execution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards and swaps may be used to hedge documented forecast or committed commercial exposures, subject to the bank's suitability, appropriateness, collateral, and credit requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available for currencies subject to local convertibility restrictions, but are not a substitute for checking the relevant jurisdiction's exchange-control rules and must be supported by a legitimate exposure and appropriate bank documentation.

Cross-currency and interest-rate swaps may be available for financing or long-term exposure management, subject to documentation, counterparty limits, valuation, collateral, and applicable EU derivatives rules.

FX options may be available where the company understands the premium, contingent exposure, and potential accounting consequences; speculative trading should be prohibited or separately authorized by a documented treasury policy.

Assess EMIR clearing, reporting, risk-mitigation, and margin requirements as applicable to the instrument and counterparty, together with MiFID II client-classification and conduct requirements. Obtain appropriate master documentation, commonly an ISDA agreement or bank standard terms, and maintain hedge designation and accounting records where hedge accounting is intended.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (Cuentas Anuales) in the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) at the registered office address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within six months of the year-end; filing within one month of approval. For calendar-year SL: approve by 30 June, deposit by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine between EUR 1,500 and EUR 60,000; suspension of good-standing certificates and registry filings; three consecutive non-filings trigger registry strike-off (cierre registral).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1–25 July following a calendar-year tax period; adjusted for different year-ends under tax law.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 5%–20% plus late interest; administrative penalties up to 150% of the assessed liability for inaccurate or omitted data.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (Registro de Titularidad Real) accompanying the annual accounts; updated within 15 days of any change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry via the annual accounts deposit; beneficial-owner data centralised at the Ministry of Justice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted at each annual accounts deposit (calendar-year: by 31 July); any change of beneficial owners must be recorded within 15 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Infringement under Law 10/2010: fines from EUR 600 to EUR 6,000 per violation; false filings treated as serious offence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual inventory report required for the free-trade-zone bonded warehouse licence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: AEAT Customs Office (Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales) at the supervising free-zone authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the close of the annual accounting period; for calendar-year operators, by 31 January.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Customs administrative penalties; liability for accrued customs debt; revocation or suspension of the bonded-depot authorisation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive years in an SL: balance-sheet total > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average staff > 50. Audit also compulsory for entities exercising exclusively public activities, listed groups, and certain regulated financial entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad) and the Commercial Code; IFRS permitted for consolidated financial statements of groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: SLs must keep an up-to-date register of beneficial owners and confirm the same at the annual accounts deposit. The beneficial-owner identification threshold includes direct or indirect ownership of 25% of capital or voting rights. No separate annual form if the annual accounts already contain the declaration; any transfer requires filing an updated register entry within 15 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Libro de Titularidad Real)
Annual Accounts and Inventory Ledger (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – 800 per year in Spain, including registered address, mail forwarding, and registry formalities.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 – 5,000 for a threshold-exceeding SL of similar size; free-zone customs auditing may add USD 2,000 – 4,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% statutory rate with R&D tax credits (up to 25% of qualifying expenses) and other preferential deductions; no general tax holidays for bonded warehouse operations

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 - Corporate Income Tax Return, filed electronically via AEAT portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 25 days after end of fiscal year (25 January for calendar year taxpayers)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductions and adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents include worldwide income attributable to Spanish PE or fixed base; file Form 210 for WHT and treaty relief

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding taxes on dividends, interest and royalties paid to non-residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents claim credit for WHT paid on Spanish-source payments

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 60 euros per day of delay (maximum 1,800 euros); 1% per month of tax due for late payment

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form 210 to AEAT with supporting documentation and Treaty Relief Certificate (TRC) to invoke DTA reduced rates
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% statutory (reduced by DTA, typically 0-10%); Interest: 19% statutory (reduced by DTA, often 0% under EU or specific treaties)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain enforces Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) under national law and EU DAC6; bonded warehouse operators must demonstrate adequate local employees, premises and core income-generating activities

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or overstatement of deductible expenses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: fines 100-200% of evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors face personal criminal liability, disqualification and imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's length pricing without Local File documentation for transactions exceeding €250,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties of 100% of tax adjustment; restitution of evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint and several liability for tax deficiencies; fines and management disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or paying royalties/interest without deducting and remitting WHT to tax authorities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines 100-200% of unpaid WHT; possible criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal payment obligation; risk of imprisonment for willful non-compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without sufficient economic substance (employees, premises, decision-making functions)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income recharacterization; loss of bonded warehouse benefits; fines up to €1 million
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Imprisonment for fraudulent conduct; disqualification from directorships
